name: National communism in Romania
summary: Romanian national communism was the quasi-official ideology of the Romanian Communist Party from the early 1960s to 1989. It kept Marxist-Leninist one-party rule, state ownership and central planning while rejecting Soviet direction in the name of national sovereignty, and made the Romanian nation, its ancient continuity and its leader the centre of political argument. Under Ceausescu it combined heavy industrialisation, a pronatalist family policy, a personality cult, Romanianisation of minorities and strict security control.
scope: The ruling-party ideology of Gheorghiu-Dej's 1964 declaration of independence and Ceausescu's rule (1965-1989), including the July Theses of 1971, Dacian and protochronist historiography, Decree 770 and the austerity of the 1980s. Excludes the internationalist Stalinist phase of the late 1940s and 1950s, the broader family of national communism elsewhere (see national-communism), and post-1989 nationalist currents. Many answers are inferred from regime practice since the party never used the label and no single canonical text exists.

universal-healthcare.rationale: A state-socialist system with nationalised services implies state-guaranteed health care, though the sources read do not describe the health system itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were set centrally by the plan; a statutory minimum wage debate does not map onto the regime, and the sources are silent.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The regime tightened central controls and refused economic liberalisation, rejecting market allocation in favour of the plan.

public-ownership.rationale: All banks and large businesses were nationalised on 11 June 1948 and heavy industry and energy stayed in state hands.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Private wealth was largely abolished, so taxing the rich was not a live policy; the sources do not address it.

unions-good.rationale: Unions existed as party-controlled transmission belts, so an adherent would praise labour organisation yet not independent unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Banks, industry and most farmland were nationalised or collectivised, treating private property as overridable by the socialist state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Private corporations hardly existed; the state owned enterprises directly, so the question of regulating them is moot.

cut-welfare.rationale: A regime that promoted full employment and state provision would see welfare cuts as contrary to socialism, though austerity hit consumption in the 1980s.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership was vested in the state and party, not in workers collectively; cooperatives and workers' ownership were not the model.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Securitate ran mass surveillance of the population as a normal tool of the party-state.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the regime's puritanical, disciplinarian social line; no source discusses drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: the 1948 constitution banned fascist or anti-democratic associations and the regime restricted speech broadly, but hate speech law as such is not documented.

strong-leader.rationale: Propaganda presented Ceausescu as a genius leader and power concentrated in him personally, bypassing any institutional check.

state-harmful.rationale: The regime strengthened the party-state and fused party and state structures; the state's withering away was no practical aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from a state that monopolised arms and distrusted private armament; no source addresses gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Securitate and security apparatus were central instruments of rule and were overhauled and strengthened after 1978.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the regime's official moralism and pronatalism; prostitution was not tolerated in the official order.

decide-locally.rationale: Systematization and party-state fusion centralised decisions, down to demolishing villages by central order.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred only; the regime stressed re-education but also harsh punishment, and the sources read do not settle it.

traditional-family.rationale: Decree 770 restricted abortion and divorce to raise the birth rate and honoured mothers of ten children as heroines.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the regime's pro-natalist family policy; no source addresses it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Decree 770 of 1966 restricted abortion and contraception sharply, leading to illegal abortions.

more-religion-public.rationale: The state promoted Marxist-Leninist atheism and nationalised church property, though it co-opted the Orthodox Church.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: the regime denied special minority claims and treated Roma as not a co-inhabiting nationality; racial-injustice remedies were not on its agenda.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the regime's biologically framed pronatalism and mother-heroine cult.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: National tradition became central: the regime absorbed the whole Romanian heritage and rehabilitated Iorga and other national figures.

gradual-change.rationale: The regime pursued forced transformation, such as systematization and collectivisation, rather than gradual change respecting old institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Policy discouraged emigration, and immigration barely existed; inferred nationalist homogenisation implies restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1964 statement asserts equality of parties and no hierarchy; Romania resisted supranational direction in Comecon and the Warsaw Pact.

free-trade.rationale: Romania rejected Comecon's specialisation plan and pursued autarkic industrialisation, though it also joined GATT to trade with the West.

nation-first.rationale: Romania rejected the Brezhnev Doctrine and Soviet interference and put its independence and national power ahead of bloc cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Ceausescu condemned the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia as a violation of sovereignty; intervention abroad contradicted his doctrine.

open-borders.rationale: Emigration was tightly controlled and nationalism was central, making open borders contrary to the regime.

limit-growth.rationale: The regime pursued breakneck industrialisation, such as huge steel and petrochemical plants, with no thought of limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the regime's industrial priorities; the issue was anachronistic in its time.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: imports of foreign technology surged and modernisation through industry was an aim, but no source states a view on technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from self-sufficiency in energy and large energy projects; the sources read do not mention nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: A communist party that came to power and legitimates itself through revolution accepts it in principle, though it opposed unauthorised upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: The party leadership decided; neither technocratic experts nor public held the real say, and the sources do not settle it.

central-planning.rationale: Central controls were tightened under Ceausescu and investment was directed by the plan to large industrial projects.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets even among public firms were rejected; the regime refused economic liberalisation and kept central command.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred; not part of Marxist-Leninist state-ownership doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from socialist hostility to inherited wealth, though personal property remained.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: the regime guaranteed work rather than unconditional cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Autarkic industrialisation and trade planning protected domestic industry by state monopoly of foreign trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: After 1974 Ceausescu directed investment into steel, petrochemicals and canal projects from the centre.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property was concentrated in the state; widely spread small ownership was not the regime's model despite private household plots.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The regime paid wages and spoke of a long-lasting socialist stage, with money abolition only a distant ideal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The state banking system was nationalised in 1948 and run as an arm of the plan.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wages and prices were set by the party-state plan, not bargained by state-recognised employer and worker bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Communist Party's leading role was written into the constitutions, and non-communist parties were forced to merge or jailed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The monarchy was abolished at the communist takeover and the regime was a republic hostile to the old order; the dynasty was condemned.

democracy-best.rationale: The regime claimed socialist democracy but ran one-party rule; liberal democracy was not held the best form.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscites were staged (e.g. the 1986 referendum), but genuine direct legislation by citizens was not the model.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils existed formally but had no real power, and the party fused with the state, so they could not be the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Romania as a unitary nation-state refused regional autonomy; the Hungarian Autonomous Region was abolished in 1968.

natural-rulers.rationale: The leadership was said to embody historical wisdom but ideology denied innate fitness for rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The regime came to power and held it by force and repression, so never is not its stance.

war-builds-character.rationale: The 1964 statement calls for lasting world peace; Romania held a defensive posture and avoided aggression.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church property was nationalised and the clergy placed under state control, though the Orthodox Church was co-opted as national.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Constitutions de jure promoted atheism and the state persecuted religious groups.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence, courts and policing were monopolised by the party-state apparatus.

military-superiority.rationale: Romania stressed defence and independence and sought status as a middle power but did not pursue superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Policy moved to nationalist homogenisation, with Hungarians and Germans cast as late-comers, though the state formally recognised co-inhabiting nationalities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism officially held it, though national continuity displaced class as the main historical frame.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Officially egalitarian, yet the nomenklatura and a dynastic family enjoyed privilege.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: no indigenous peoples policy; Roma were neglected and Hungarians denied autonomy.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The 1964 statement condemns colonialism in all forms; reparations themselves are not mentioned.

civilizational-union.rationale: Romania stressed national sovereignty and a Latin identity set apart from Slavic neighbours rather than civilisational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialist ideology held individual self-interest subordinate to collective goals.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Propaganda demanded sacrifice for the nation and party, notably austerity for debt repayment.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from an industry-first ethos that remade the landscape.

limit-population.rationale: Decree 770 aimed to raise the birth rate by banning abortion and contraception.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The regime pursued intensive industrialisation as its central goal and saw heavy industry as progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Industrialisation was driven hard, but institutional disruption was not embraced since the party kept control.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred only; no source addresses it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from party command of decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The Securitate's mass surveillance and state control of communications leave no room for unbreakable private encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The regime saw itself as building socialism and progress, though it drew on a mythic past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy was subordinated to party ideology and the leader's will even at the cost of results.

direct-action.rationale: A ruling party opposed unsanctioned direct action and put down protests such as the Brasov revolt.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed by the regime, which used coercion in the name of a socialist end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rapid industrialisation and urbanisation were central; a return to foraging is the opposite.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The plan expanded specialised industrial labour; division of labour was kept despite ideal talk.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism's final stage is by need in doctrine, but the regime ran on socialist distribution by work.

production-for-use.rationale: The plan nominally directed production to social needs, not profit, though it favoured heavy industry over consumer goods.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy holds that capitalist profit is exploitation, as the basis of nationalisation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Official doctrine held that the party rules on behalf of the working class, with repression of bourgeois opponents.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation was declared complete in 1962 with collective and state farms holding 77 percent of arable land.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The 1964 statement frames imperialism as the common enemy, in line with Leninist theory; Romania also traded with the West.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state owning the economy and collecting its revenue directly rejects this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: The party-state regulated private life, from reproduction (Decree 770) to culture, far beyond harm prevention.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Group identity of the nation and the 'co-inhabiting nationalities' were recognised, and individual rights were subordinate.

conscription.rationale: Romania kept a conscript army within the Warsaw Pact system and emphasised national defence.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emigration was discouraged by lengthy procedures, job loss and fees, so exit was not valued.

state-as-business.rationale: The state was run as a party apparatus under a leader, not on business or customer lines.

positive-liberty.rationale: Socialist doctrine holds freedom needs material means such as work and housing; the regime claimed to provide them.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and universities were controlled by the party and Council for Socialist Education, so held little independent power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninism rejected racial hierarchies; inferred as the regime's line.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation ran through party and mass organisations, not families and trade bodies as corporatist estates.

total-state.rationale: After the July Theses the party sought to direct culture, education and economy, fusing party and state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Official history told of a nation united for two thousand years and raised under Ceausescu to major-power status, though without a decadence myth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The regime stressed sovereignty and non-intervention and did not press for territorial expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority was claimed through party and state institutions, though loyalty to the leader mattered in practice.

bound-labor.rationale: Collectivisation bound peasants to cooperatives but ended feudal obligations; serfdom was condemned as past exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism-Leninism ties knowledge to class, yet claimed its own science as objective.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; official ideology claimed a materialist ethic.

single-common-good.rationale: Party doctrine presumes a single correct line serving the whole people rather than a balance of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Romania was the only bloc state with normal relations with both Israel and the PLO and helped mediate Sadat's 1977 visit; this implies acceptance of Israel's existence.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not documented; Romania claimed ties to Romanians abroad but did not issue return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Romanian was already the state language; the question of reviving a lost language does not apply.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Nominal workers' councils had little influence, with management by party appointees.

school-vouchers.rationale: Private schools were nationalised in 1948 and education was a state monopoly.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The regime restrained its finances to repay foreign debt and in 1986 barred foreign loans by constitutional amendment.

economic-freedom.rationale: The regime refused economic liberalisation and ranked political order above economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Propaganda built the leader as an exemplar but ruled through law, the Securitate and coercion.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1964 statement asserts each party's and people's right to its own path; independence was the defining principle.

force-without-un.rationale: Ceausescu denounced the 1968 intervention in Czechoslovakia and favoured non-use of force across borders.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Official materialism and atheism put science above religion, though the cult itself ran on emotion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred; few immigrants existed and the sources do not discuss welfare eligibility.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Socialist ideology obliged able citizens to work; parasitism was punishable under the regime.

class-collaboration.rationale: Marxism-Leninism views classes as opposed, though national unity around the leader was stressed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The regime absorbed the whole Romanian heritage and rehabilitated Iorga and Lovinescu rather than discarding the past.

dominated-front.rationale: Romania spoke of the equal rights of states, but did not join a common anti-Western front as it traded with the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The 1964 declaration abandoned proletarian internationalism for the national road, with the working class organised in the nation's party.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist motherhood cult; official ideology also proclaimed formal equality.

ban-interest.rationale: The state banking system charged interest as an instrument of planning; no ban was imposed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Official ideology rejected racial segregation, and the constitution guaranteed minority equality, whatever the practice.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds the state is a class instrument; used to justify the proletarian state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy self-sufficiency and the oil-heavy economy drove production; imports of oil became costly after 1979.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Romanianization pushed minorities to assimilate; immigrants themselves were rare.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this kind is alien to official ideology and unattested.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections were single-list under party control; proportional representation of competing parties was meaningless.

national-mission.rationale: The doctrine opposed imposing one system on others; the 1964 text rejects 'parent' parties and lines.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Official ideology claimed women's equality; the regime's family policy tells otherwise, and the sources do not decide.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The regime denied it, though nepotism ('dynastic socialism') was widespread; an adherent would not accept the claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Pronatalism pushed births generally; eugenic measures are not documented.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Securitate answered only to the party leadership; accountability for security abuses was contrary to the regime.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A regime that nationalised the economy and directed culture rejects minimal-state doctrine.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Official ideology rejected racism; no policy of the kind is recorded.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formal equality before the law was constitutionally proclaimed, though practised unevenly with minorities.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The 1964 declaration abandoned internationalism for a national road; Romania built socialism on its own.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial in general, but no source links this to its national case.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitutions applied one law to all citizens; Marxism-Leninism dismisses religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred only; the regime was hostile to religion rather than regulating conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Meat was produced and exported for debt service; a ban would run against the economy.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church schools were nationalised in 1948 and the state promoted atheism in education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The party-state grew stronger and fused with party structures under Ceausescu, and security forces were reinforced, rather than withering away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rule claimed popular legitimacy through staged elections and acclaim, but legitimacy by real consent was not applied.

trade-surplus.rationale: Exports of food and industrial output were boosted to repay debt, so running a surplus was the declared aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Policy steered Romanians into minority cities and minorities out, and Germans and Jews were allowed to leave for payment; coercive transfer itself is not documented.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A regime born of revolution and resting on repression rejects an absolute pacifist rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Socialist ideology prefers planned cooperation, though nationalism cast peoples as rivals in history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 1948 constitution banned associations of a fascist or anti-democratic nature, applied against any opposition party.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of freedom is not addressed in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Ceausescu called for blending party and state activities and joint bodies fused functions instead of separating powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Communist Party held a leading role written into the constitutions as the vanguard of the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialist ideology claims to prioritise working people; the privileged nomenklatura contradicted it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: State housing was built through high-density apartment blocks; apartments were often sold later but the sources do not cover it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were not recognised in the party-state, and the 1987 Brasov revolt was suppressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Decree 770 and the pronatalist drive treated large populations as an asset, not a cause of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Romanianization campaign treated minority distinctiveness as a threat to national unity, notably for Hungarians.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were filled by party cadre appointment through the nomenklatura.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The security apparatus acted without legal restraint against dissent, with surveillance as routine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices were fixed by the state; during the 1980s austerity bread, meat and heating were rationed.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Securitate controlled the media, and the July Theses put propaganda into media and the arts.

party-commands-army.rationale: The party leadership commanded the armed forces; Ceausescu held supreme command as party leader.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism bound members to party decisions as in all ruling Leninist parties.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from nationalist homogenisation; citizenship by immigration was not a live matter.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Doctrine preached modest pay for officials, practice was privileged; the sources do not settle it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The 1964 statement insists each party and state decides for itself with no one imposing a line; Romania refused supranational direction.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Ceausescu united the offices of party leader and president and commanded the armed forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Orthodox Church kept its episcopal structure under state control, but the regime had no doctrine on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state promoted atheism and persecuted religious groups; clerical rule is the opposite of its constitution.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's doctrine, but Romania as a state stressed national defence and sovereignty and never encouraged defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: After the July Theses writers were pushed back to Socialist Realism and ideological conformity demanded.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ceausescu was re-elected as party leader and president repeatedly, without limit, until 1989.

recall-officials.rationale: Formal recall by electors existed in socialist constitutions but had no role in practice.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Romania stayed in the Warsaw Pact while limiting its role; it did not leave nor end alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The state built blocks of flats allocated by the state; owner-only housing was not policy.

people-in-arms.rationale: Romania maintained patriotic guards as a people's militia alongside the army; inferred and not directly documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Systematization demolished villages for apartment blocs and urbanised the workforce; rural idealisation was not state doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The regime championed national unity in history, framing Bessarabia and Transylvania as part of Romanian unification, though state policy did not claim Bessarabia.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The regime courted intellectuals through national culture but disciplined them after the July Theses; it did not claim this populist line.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Official ideology set Romanians as a Latin island with continuous achievement, so cultures were not seen as simply equal.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime used the death penalty for grave crimes and political cases; inferred as accepted practice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Contraception was restricted, so sex education was discouraged in line with the pronatalist policy.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The state promoted materialist atheism in education, so creationism is rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Strict moral and ideological control of culture implies restricting pornography; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Romanians were defined as a nation of continuous descent from Dacians and Romans, which fits descent-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: The constitution promised mother-tongue education but under Ceausescu Hungarian and German schools and media were merged or curtailed, and signs removed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state persecuted religious groups and offered no exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity was demanded after the July Theses and the cult required uniform praise.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Romania sought rescheduling in 1981 and then repaid in full; it supported debt relief for poor countries only in general anti-imperialist terms.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1964 statement links anti-colonial struggle with the socialist transformation; independence meant economic autonomy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutions were written under party control; the issue of democratic constituent assemblies was not addressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The party restricted freedoms for forced industrialisation and austerity to repay debt.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The 1964 statement affirms the common anti-colonial struggle; Romania sought development ties with the Third World.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Romania stayed under the Warsaw Pact umbrella and did not seek an independent nuclear deterrent, though it valued independence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was chosen by the legislature on party direction, not directly elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The banking system was nationalised in 1948 and subject to the plan, so central bank independence was rejected.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Romania did not claim lost territory officially, yet the national narrative treated unity as sacred; the regime also signed away nothing.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist doctrine allows property only in service of the collective; private ownership was subordinate to the socialist state.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Romania's party considered the USSR a socialist state, in dispute over line not over character; Ceausescu's break was about independence.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources show no concern for environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Romania joined the Warsaw Pact in 1955 with its collective defence clause, though it limited participation later.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Official history called the union with Transylvania an occupation in the 1950s, but later the position reversed; no clear stance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church property was nationalised in 1948, the Greek-Catholic Church was disbanded into the Orthodox, and clergy placed under state oversight.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceausescu was simultaneously party general secretary and president, the opposite of a nonpartisan head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: A unitary nation-state that abolished the Hungarian Autonomous Region would resist separation; not directly documented.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy was hollowed out and then abolished in 1968, with the Hungarian region redrawn to reduce its share.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The cult made Ceausescu a genius and a successor to Stephen the Great, but not sacred or of divine descent in a materialist state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from socialist taxation; the state took its revenue by enterprise and not flat income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist-Leninist materialism holds character is formed by circumstance, behind the 'new man' project.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The leader stood above the law in practice, with no constitutional check on his rule.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The party monopolised power, and mixed rule by few and many contradicts the single-party constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: By the 1980s propaganda portrayed Ceausescu as a genius and heroic successor to Stephen the Great, with portraits and mass praise.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; family law under Decree 770 favoured intact families.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Official line held class enemies persisted, but Romania's leadership did not accept leaders themselves might restore capitalism in the Maoist sense.

land-redistribution.rationale: A 1945 land reform preceded collectivisation, with big estates broken up, though the later aim was collective farming.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; policy discouraged emigration and refugee return was no issue.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The 1964 statement upholds sovereignty and non-interference; Romania criticised Hungarian interest in Transylvanian Hungarians as interference.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Constitutions de jure promoted atheism and the regime did not punish leaving religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Nothing in the regime's secular, anti-religious doctrine would support compulsory covering.

common-currency.rationale: National sovereignty was central, and trade was conducted by state monopoly in national currency within Comecon's transferable rouble limits.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The nation was seen as a Latin island, apart from Slavic neighbours; political union with kin peoples was not pursued.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The constitution promised minority schools and institutions but they were merged with Romanian ones; the stance was formal in words and denied in practice.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not a question the regime addressed; it let Germans and Jews emigrate for payment, but opposed Hungarian ties abroad.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism remained official doctrine, even as nationalism entered it.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state monopolised industry in planned combines, making antitrust irrelevant.

no-bailouts.rationale: State firms were backed by the plan; the question hardly arose.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The party-state saw no external constraint on its majority will; courts were subordinate to it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women were represented formally in the party and bodies, but parity by law was not policy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ceausescu pursued autarkic industrialisation and, after 1981, a strict no-foreign-loans line; however Romania traded with the West.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; Romania defended its sovereignty in trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: The regime relied on ideological education, socialist emulation and calls for sacrifice, in the model of Maoist and North Korean practice Ceausescu admired.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The party opposed adventurism, since it ruled in a established party-state.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The monarchy and aristocracy were abolished, though Ceausescu's family itself held hereditary-like power.

history-own-civilization.rationale: After the 1964 turn history was rewritten with the Romanian nation at its centre, in the Dacian narrative.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1964 statement rejects any 'parent' party or state over another, and anti-colonialism ran through its foreign policy.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism became the central political argument and Romanians were depicted as united around the Leader, taught in schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed in the regime context; preferences did not exist as policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money was created by the nationalised state bank rather than private banks lending.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninism predicts capitalist crisis, though Romania traded with the West.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The 1950s history opposed this, later nationalist history stressed Dacian and Roman glory without a policy of regional empire influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Ceausescu joined the IMF and GATT and sought Western credit, so not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist idea, but Romania's party-state did not take it up as a theme in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The state banned private discrimination as a principle; private owners were not free in economic matters.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights were proclaimed in constitutions the party could change at will; entrenched limits on government were rejected.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonialism in the 1964 statement implies it; no source states this.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers were chosen by the party leadership and not through competitive elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism requires decisions bind dissenting minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The regime crushed dissent and the Securitate suppressed resistance; the doctrine denied any right to resist.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The party, not parliament, held supreme power; the Grand National Assembly rubber-stamped decisions.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No source read touches animal welfare; the regime's industrial and agricultural drive gave it no visible place.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from a state that ran farming and research for output; the sources read say nothing on animal treatment.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialist ideology rejects aristocratic duty and abolished privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The regime demanded mass political participation and ideological education of all citizens.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist critique, but the regime itself used mass culture for propaganda and did not endorse the critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian argument not addressed in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The anti-imperialist common struggle in the 1964 statement covers neo-colonial exploitation; Romania also advocated a new international economic order.

native-born-offices.rationale: Ethnic Romanians dominated party membership and key posts; inferred nationalism favours native offices.

party-own-road.rationale: The 1964 statement says parties work in varied conditions, none is a 'parent' party, and no party may impose its line on others.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: After 1981 Romania repaid its foreign debt, and the 1986 amendment banned foreign loans, but earlier it borrowed heavily.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Official line never demanded Bessarabia's return officially, as it would clash with the USSR, though nationalists in the party hinted at it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism was an official founding value of the communist state, even as Antonescu was semi-rehabilitated as a patriot.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The regime rejected equating communism with fascism, with the 1948 constitution banning fascist associations as an enemy.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A question about United States history that Romanian national communism never addressed; neutral by default.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The regime built monuments to its own leader and rehabilitated older national figures while erasing others; no stable line.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Regime policy centred on pronatalism and class, and the sources read never discuss male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources read never address domestic violence, and official family policy gave it no stated place.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The 1964 statement affirms each country's own conditions and national road; this extends to political forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party commanded the army; the army was not to act as an independent guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Mothers were honoured by title but domestic work was not paid; the regime stayed silent.

filial-duty.rationale: The family was seen as the basis of society in regime policy; filial duty was part of its moral order.

office-by-exam.rationale: Party loyalty governed selection, but exams were used in education; unclear.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State control of the economy barred foreign ownership and the 1986 amendment limited foreign ties.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recall was formal only; it had no real role.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions were a state matter in a nationalised system, so private pension accounts are rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was nationalised or collectivised with farmers holding household plots, matching state or community holding of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A rubber-stamp assembly approved budgets formally; effective parliamentary control was absent.

single-official-language.rationale: Romanian was the state language; Hungarian and German schools and signs were curtailed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land was impossible under state and cooperative holding.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; the regime did not recognise group-disparity claims for Roma or Hungarians.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Austerity and rationing, plus emphasis on heavy industry over consumer goods and moral incentives, point to a hostility to consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Romania's line was non-intervention; however it supported national liberation movements in general.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Romania rejected the Brezhnev Doctrine and Soviet interference in allied states, condemning the 1968 invasion.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not applicable to a state without private corporate lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The Securitate controlled foreign contacts and funding; independent organisations had no foreign support.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Decree 770 offered benefits for large families and the title of heroine mother to mothers of ten or more children.

residents-only-property.rationale: Property was state or cooperative, so local residency limits on purchase had no counterpart; the sources are silent.

job-guarantee.rationale: The regime guaranteed employment, moving workers from farms to factories as a core socialist promise.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the regime did not endorse democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The regime demanded obedience to party and leader, backed by the Securitate.

non-intervention.rationale: The 1964 statement rejects imposing lines on other parties, and in 1968 Ceausescu condemned the Czechoslovakia invasion as a violation of sovereignty.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trade unions in socialist states were organised by branch of industry; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hungarians were suspected as irredentists, but the regime formally rejected conspiratorial ethnic theories.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Decree 770 and family policy treated marriage as a state-backed institution to maintain.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Securitate and censorship controlled information, with no right of access to government records.

local-production.rationale: Large centralised combines and plants were built; local production was not an aim.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party monopolised organisation and forbade independent groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The doctrine of sovereignty and non-interference puts national law first.

religious-nation.rationale: The state was atheist, though the Orthodox Church was folded into a national narrative.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Romania rejected Soviet leadership and the Brezhnev Doctrine, resisting any ritual deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Central planning pooled revenue; Ceausescu centralised decisions in the capital.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal belongings, homes and household plots stayed private under socialism while the means of production were collective.

defeat-communism.rationale: A ruling communist party obviously rejects it; Romania held to coexistence with the West and the existing socialist system.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Services were delivered solely by the state after the 1948 nationalisation of church schools and firms.

religion-illusion.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninism held religion to be an illusion that would fade, with state promotion of atheism, though tactical tolerance of Orthodoxy.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds capitalism built the material basis for socialism, as Romanian Marxist historiography does.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist doctrine ties women's equality to socialist economic transformation, as in the regime's claims.

socialized-care.rationale: Official socialist policy provided state nurseries and care, though not directly documented in the sources read.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Romanianization changed place names (Cluj to Cluj-Napoca) but no purge of loanwords is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: Concerns treaties with nations inside a state's borders; Romania's doctrine addressed inter-state sovereignty, not this.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Systematization instead concentrated people in large blocks and demolished villages.

majority-settlement.rationale: Migration was steered so that Romanians moved into minority cities while minorities were pushed out.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The regime considered itself communist and socialist; a third way was rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Official history after 1964 built the case for continuous Romanian presence from the Dacians in Transylvania.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Antonescu was semi-rehabilitated as a misunderstood patriot, but the regime did not officially deny the Holocaust; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Romanian law criminalised homosexual acts under Article 200 through the regime's period; inferred as regime policy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Securitate carried out mass surveillance and severe repression, and non-communist parties were forced to merge or jailed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: State atheism meant no protection for blasphemy law or the practice of 'false religion'.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The 1964 statement condemns colonialism in all its forms.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A specifically Islamic doctrine outside the regime's frame, and the sources read never touch it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not compatible with a state that promoted atheism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participation was staged and controlled; ordinary people did not shape decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; class was the official category.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the regime's moral conservatism; no source addresses it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from pronatalist valuing of life; no source addresses it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The party saw itself as the left and rejected 'beyond left and right'.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist claim about capitalism that official doctrine upheld.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The sources read never address Islam or Western culture; a secular atheist state had no stated line on this.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The state promoted atheism, so authority derives from the party and people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from a secular state hostile to religion in public institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contracts in a state-employer economy had no equivalent, and the sources are silent on it.

social-market-economy.rationale: The regime refused liberalisation and kept the command economy, not a market economy with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Romania kept a conscript army and emphasised national defence and sovereignty.

rich-first.rationale: Socialist ideology rejects letting some grow rich first, unlike the Chinese reform line.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Romania stayed in the Warsaw Pact formally but acted independently, opening to the West; it neither left nor stayed fully aligned.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ceausescu groomed his son and placed relatives in power, 'dynastic socialism', though not as official doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit was issued by the state banking system under the plan.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Romania repaid its debt through its own austerity and later barred foreign loans; it resisted IMF-style supervision.

property-franchise.rationale: Universal suffrage was nominal; property qualifications ran against socialist doctrine.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme of regime ideology, which sought to master nature through industry.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept accepted in doctrine though absent from the regime's practice.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Standard Marxist-Leninist critique used to justify party control of the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule by decree and the leader's will prevailed, not constraint by standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Constitutions proclaimed universal rights regardless of nationality.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from control of information.

open-government-data.rationale: Censorship and secrecy governed state information.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The secular state did not restrict religious intermarriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Private shops were nationalised and ethnic boycotts were not part of official policy.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Party-led bodies, not randomly selected citizens, were used to deliberate.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Official doctrine treated religion as an illusion to fade, so reinterpreting it was not a regime concern.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Standard socialist claim against private wealth, though the regime concentrated power elsewhere.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred; same-sex acts were criminal in the period.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state de jure promoted Marxist-Leninist atheism, though the Orthodox Church was co-opted in practice.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Securitate and prison system were pillars of the regime.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Minority representation was nominal and Romanians dominated posts; no communal power-sharing existed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The socialist state claimed responsibility for welfare and nationalised church institutions.

term-limits.rationale: Ceausescu stayed leader for decades with no limit on terms.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not compatible with the single-list election system.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic concern with no counterpart in the sources read; the regime's priorities were industry and national power.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Official equality in family law is claimed; Decree 770 limited choice, so weak.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Foreign residents had no say in a party-state.

rent-control.rationale: Rents were state-set in nationalised housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property law is not discussed in the sources read; socialist states held state-owned inventions but did not campaign on it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The regime built the Pioneers and Falcons of the Fatherland as party youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Romania stressed sovereignty and did not host Soviet nuclear missiles by choice in public statements; also joined disarmament proposals.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Romania refused Warsaw Pact maneuvers on its soil and rejected Soviet interference, hosting no Soviet troops after 1958.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Socialist principle distributes by labour; unearned income from ownership was abolished.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A state with a standing army and the right to defence rejects this.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Official ideology portrayed Romanians as a Latin island that preserved unity and independence for two thousand years, from Dacians on.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; the pronatalist line assumes biological sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; women were treated as a category (mothers and workers).

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The regime honoured national heroes and 'great leaders' throughout history, with fallen heroes cherished.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Materialist doctrine denies politics as spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Romania claimed unity with Romanians beyond its borders in national history, though not on a diaspora policy basis.

culture-before-state.rationale: The state was built first and imposed culture through the July Theses.

god-not-male.rationale: A theological question on which the atheist state took no position, and the sources read never raise it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist-theological claim that the regime never addressed; its official stance on religion was atheism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The economy was state-owned; ethnic ownership was not an issue.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Hungarian Autonomous Region was redrawn in 1960 and abolished in 1968, so merging regions for a people was rejected.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions were controlled by the party; independence was not tolerated.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The regime claimed to be a workers' state, though the party elite held real power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water, hospitals and transport were state-run.

second-chamber.rationale: The Grand National Assembly was unicameral, from the 1965 constitution.

municipal-property.rationale: Means of production belonged to the state, not local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Centralisation was the principle, so confederal local coordination was rejected.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy and family allowances aimed to support families as part of pronatalism; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Pharmaceutical regulation is not covered in the sources read; the state ran health and drug supply centrally.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic for the period and not discussed in the sources read; neutral by default.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State control of money flows and surveillance are incompatible with anonymous payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Securitate's surveillance.

person-over-state.rationale: The person was subordinate to party and nation, as Ceausescu's austerity and systematization show.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional autonomy lasted only at the centre's pleasure; the Hungarian Autonomous Region was abolished in 1968.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering was not a live issue in the regime's era, and the sources read do not mention it.

dense-cities.rationale: Systematization built high-density apartment blocks and razed villages; environmental rationale was not the driver.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; national pride rather than racial pride was the framework.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Romania stressed defence, sovereignty and peace and condemned aggression.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Romanians as a Latin people united by language and descent are the basis of the national narrative, though Romania also recognised co-inhabiting nationalities.

communal-electorates.rationale: Elections were single list; communal electorates not used.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Official nationalism portrayed outside forces against Romanian unity, and Soviet and Hungarian pressures; inferred and partly documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher education was free under the state system; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; industrial output was prioritised.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The pronatalist cult honoured mothers, but there was no doctrine of distinct women's values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: The 1964 statement calls for a lasting peace, and Romania advocated disarmament while keeping defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The regime's diplomacy was personalised in the leader and the party secrecy; open diplomacy was not a principle.

capital-controls.rationale: After 1981 Romania cut imports, controlled hard-currency flows and then banned foreign loans, along with state monopoly of foreign trade.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The party-state kept command of the armed forces and Securitate, though it also ran party-controlled Patriotic Guards, so the monopoly was loose in form (inferred).

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A one-party regime that demanded discipline and national defence would not endorse soldiers refusing orders; Romania refused Warsaw Pact action in 1968 as a state decision, not a soldiers' one.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions were party-controlled bodies and wages were set by the plan, so independent bargaining did not exist (inferred).

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wages and incomes were administered by the central plan, so this market-economy tool does not fit (inferred).

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The regime sought to eliminate foreign debt in the 1980s at great cost, which suggests sympathy for strict limits on borrowing, though it ran a planned economy, not legal fiscal rules (inferred).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Romania presented itself as a developing socialist country and defended national economic sovereignty against both blocs, but the sources do not give a restructuring programme (inferred).

smash-state-machine.rationale: The party ruled through the existing state and strengthened it, so replacing it was not an aim.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The regime enforced central planning and state ownership under one party, with no room for different local systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; the regime treated natural resources as inputs for planned heavy industrialisation, not as priced capital (inferred).

sacred-nation.rationale: National communism put the Romanian nation, its ancient continuity and its leader at the centre of its ideology, which is close to treating the nation as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; higher education was state-funded and there was no student loan system.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The regime held the nation as one unit and rejected regional or minority claims of exploitation, while Romanianising minority areas (inferred).

shared-human-nature.rationale: The regime promoted the idea of the 'new socialist man' and social engineering, which points away from a fixed human nature (inferred).

public-service-media.rationale: Press, radio and television were under party censorship and served as instruments of the leader's cult, so independent public media was the opposite of the regime's practice.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist state was officially atheist and subordinated the churches, though it did not teach that religions are one truth; inferred from regime practice.

farm-price-support.rationale: State collectivisation and state purchase of farm output were regime policy; inferred from socialist agricultural planning.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Ceausescu pursued disarmament rhetoric while keeping a nuclear research programme; the regime never held weapons, so the question is not settled by sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: One-party rule barred independent parties of any class; the Romanian Communist Party claimed to be the workers' party itself.

ban-fgm.rationale: Formal equality of women was official doctrine, though the regime was strongly pronatalist; inferred, not from a source on FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The socialist state proclaimed legal equality of women, so equal inheritance fits; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Official nationalist historiography treated Romanians in Moldova as one nation and language; inferred from the nation-centred ideology.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Central planning and state ownership leave enforcement to the state, not private tort suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A one-party centralised state would not give customary chiefs lawmaking roles; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Heavy industrialisation was prioritised over environmental limits, and individual liberty was not at stake in the regime's view; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A strict security state favours fixed, severe penalties; inferred from regime practice, not a stated source.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The regime's Romanianisation of minorities (s3) implies expecting Romanian language use by all residents; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Under the one-party system trade unions were run as state-controlled transmission belts, so membership was effectively an assumed part of employment rather than voluntary.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; elections were uncompetitive single-list affairs and identification rules were not a political issue.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from regime practice: the Orthodox Church was favored while the Greek-Catholic Church had been suppressed, so interpretations were not treated equally.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The regime claimed a 'socialist democracy' under single-party rule, which rejects the idea that competitive elections define democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Ceausescu's pronatalist family policy and puritanical official morality, including Decree 770; not directly stated in the sources read.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the regime's security control and censorship; the issue is anachronistic for the period.

negative-income-tax.rationale: State ownership and central planning defined the economy, so replacing welfare programs with a market-style cash payment is contrary to its principles.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution of the socialist republic gave women equal political rights and women sat in the legislature and party bodies, though real power was held by a few.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: official Marxism-Leninism was atheist but the regime tolerated and used the Orthodox Church, so no consistent line on religion as a cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: official policy stressed Romanian national continuity, not biological race, and the sources read do not address whether races are constructs.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from official women's organizations of the party-state; the sources do not describe dedicated ministries.

missingStatements.text: A government should repay its foreign debts in full even if it requires severe austerity for its own people.
missingStatements.rationale: Ceausescu cut imports, rationed energy and food and exported output through the 1980s to clear Romania's foreign debt, then barred foreign loans by constitutional amendment.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Ceausescu's debt policy; the issue is covered from the other side by sovereign-debt-cancellation and refuse-lender-austerity.

missingStatements.text: The state may demolish villages and move rural people into planned high-density towns.
missingStatements.rationale: Systematization from 1974 razed villages and old city districts for apartment blocks, and a rural resettlement drive began in 1988.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to Romanian systematization; related collective-farming and land-use questions already exist.

notes: Gheorghiu-Dej's 1964 line was milder and more reformist than Ceausescu's post-1971 turn toward cult, cultural control and austerity; this profile follows the Ceausescu mainstream. The 1964 statement itself addresses relations among parties, so many domestic positions are inferred from regime practice.
